---
title: Notebooks
---

## Overview

Quarto renders a Jupyter notebook (`.ipynb`) directly — there is no need to
convert it to a `.qmd` file first:

```bash
quarto render penguins.ipynb
```

Each cell of the notebook becomes part of the rendered document:

- **Markdown cells** render as Quarto markdown. A cell may open a fence or
  callout that a later cell closes — structure can span cells, exactly as it
  would in a `.qmd` document.
- **Code cells** show their source as a code block, followed by their
  outputs.
- **Raw cells** whose `raw_mimetype` is `text/html` render that HTML; other
  raw cells are shown as plain code.

## Stored outputs are the document

By default, Quarto renders the outputs *stored in the notebook* — stream
text, rich results (including HTML tables and plots), and error output. This
requires no Python or Jupyter installation: the notebook is its own record of
the computation, and rendering just shows it.

Plots stored as PNG are written as figure files alongside the rendered
document, so they participate in figure numbering and cross-references like
any other Quarto figure.

## Re-running the computation

To *execute* the notebook's code instead of replaying its stored outputs, ask
for execution — from the notebook's front matter:

````markdown
---
execute:
  enabled: true
---
````

or with `quarto render penguins.ipynb --execute`. Execution goes through the
[Jupyter engine](engines.qmd), so it requires a working Jupyter installation.
A notebook that demands execution is always executed — it is never silently
replaced by its stored outputs.

## Front matter and titles

A notebook supplies document metadata the same way a `.qmd` does:

- If the first raw or markdown cell begins with YAML front matter
  (`---` delimiters), that cell is the document's front matter.
- Otherwise, if the first markdown cell is nothing but a top heading, that
  heading becomes the document's `title` and the remaining lines of the cell
  stay in the body.
- Notebook-level metadata (the notebook's `metadata` field) merges into the
  document metadata as well.

## Errors point at cells

When Quarto reports a problem inside a notebook — a markdown parse error, an
invalid option, a bad `#|` chunk option in a code cell — the message names
the cell it came from:

```text
Error: notebook.ipynb[cell 3, code] line 2, column 1: ...
```

Cells are numbered from 1, counting every cell regardless of type, and the
line and column are relative to the start of that cell.
